item: The deferred PowerShell row goes to its child on standard input, never in the command line (passphrase rule)
summary: The first R174 build started the PowerShell child with -EncodedCommand carrying the row (as base64 inside the script): a command line is visible to every local user in a process listing, and with script block logging on Windows the decoded command reaches the event log; a stderr row carries whatever the server printed. Now the child is started with one fixed script and the path, the limits and the row are written to its standard input as UTF-8 bytes, then the pipe is closed. Pinned: two rows with different pids, times and folders give the identical decoded script, and it holds no field of the row and no folder (red on the first build); the bash child is pinned the same way with a marker assembled at run time and a scan of every process command line while the row waits (flock and mkdir lock): the row stays in the memory of the subshell. Never run on PowerShell 5.1 or a real Windows console.
